name: MoGe
plain: Microsoft's MoGe: depth, 3D points, normals and focal length from one image.
summary: MoGe-2 / MoGe-3 (Wang et al., Microsoft): monocular metric geometry; a DINOv2 ViT with conv heads predicts an affine point map, a validity mask, normals and a metric scale, and the focal length and shift are recovered from the points (MoGe-3 adds a sparse 3-D refiner).

papers.title: MoGe-2: Accurate Monocular Geometry with Metric Scale and Sharp Details
MoGe-3: Fine-Detail Monocular Geometry Estimation with Self-Guided Sparse Volumetric Refinement

task_io: Input: one RGB image. Output: a depth or inverse-depth map. `kind` (a card field, `result.kind`) says what the numbers mean: `metric` = metres; `scale_invariant`, `affine_invariant` and `affine_invariant_inverse` are relative (unknown scale or shift, not metres). Metric models that use the focal length take `model(image, intrinsics=K)` (K `[3, 3]`, pixels of the input): `metric3d-vit-large` and `da3metric-large` need it for correct metres (`da3metric-large`: metres = output x focal / 300; without `intrinsics=` a 300 px focal length is assumed, wrong for a real camera). `unidepth-v2-vitl14`, `unik3d-vitl`, `depth-pro` and MoGe estimate the camera themselves (given `intrinsics=` replace `fx`); `zoedepth-nk` and the relative models (`da3mono-large` too) take none. Normals-only models (`kind` `none`) return `result.normals` `[B, H, W, 3]` (unit vectors, camera frame: x right, y down, z forward).

parity.text: CPU, float32: max |diff| <= 0.005 vs the original. GPU, float16 (the default), portable and kernels: mean |diff| <= 1.5 % and p99 <= 1.5 % of the reference's median |value| (absolute error of the output `depth`).
